findings.title: Error-handler parameter conflicts with process event arguments
findings.description: `index.ts` registers `handleError` directly for `uncaughtException` and `unhandledRejection`. Those events supply an origin string or Promise as their second argument, now interpreted as `exitCode`. Reproduction throws `ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE` inside `process.exit`, breaking clean error handling across the CLI. Wrap both listeners so they pass only the error, and add regression tests.

findings.title: Successful writes can produce a false validation success
findings.description: `remaining` tracks failed writes, not validation results. In `frontmatterSchema.ts`, missing `docType` produces one fixable finding and returns before checking other required fields. Consequently, a document named `100-slice.example.md` with only `status` can receive its inferred `docType` and exit successfully while still missing `slice`, `project`, and `dateCreated`. Revalidate after fixing and derive the exit status from the resulting findings. Add a real-service regression test.

findings.title: Missing-date repair can overwrite the current update timestamp
findings.description: The schema’s fix for missing `dateUpdated` uses `dateCreated`. The writer deliberately ignores the fourth argument when updating `dateUpdated` itself. If both status and `dateUpdated` need repair, the status write stamps today, then the date repair overwrites it with the creation date. Use the run’s timestamp for `dateUpdated` repairs and test the persisted result rather than only mocked arguments.
